chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), or to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'A man deliberately postpones the month in the short days, so he fasts it for a year.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem.'

key_terms.الشَّهْرَ: the month (referring to the three days of the lunar month)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to delay fasting the three white days of the month until winter?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of deferring the voluntary fasts of Ayyam al-Beed (the white days) to winter months to ensure the completion of the annual tally, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of flexibility in voluntary acts of worship. It highlights the Imam's leniency regarding the timing of these specific fasts, distinguishing them from the fixed days of Ramadan or Eid, and underscores the importance of maintaining consistent devotional habits despite seasonal variations in day length.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Hassan Bin Rashid who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, or to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man deliberately (postpones) to the month in which the days are shorter, so he Fasts these (optional Fasts) for the year’. He<sup>asws</sup> said; ‘There is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from al-Hassan ibn Rashid who has said the following:
“I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who purposely postpones fasting for the times when days of the year are shorter. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful.’”
